title: Chartwise calculus for smooth and etale representable morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. For morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$ representable by algebraic spaces, each property in the list smooth, etale, flat, locally of finite presentation, locally of finite type is stable under arbitrary base change and composition and can be checked on an open cover of the source. An open substack is a full substack whose pullback by any scheme is an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Surjectivity is stable under base change and composition. Etale morphisms are smooth, and smooth morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation; local finite presentation implies local finite type. For a set-indexed family of etale morphisms $q_i:U_i\to\mathcal X$ from schemes, the map $\coprod_iU_i\to\mathcal X$ obtained by gluing their objects along the disjoint open cover is etale and representable by algebraic spaces, provided the scheme coproduct belongs to the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Scheme properties mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Here surjectivity means field-extension local lifting: for every field $K$, every object $y$ of the target over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ admits, after an extension $K\hookrightarrow L$, a source object $x$ and an isomorphism $f(x)\simeq y|_L$. For a map representable by algebraic spaces this is equivalent to the chart test of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ and every surjective etale scheme chart $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, the scheme map $U\to T$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. An open cover means a family of open substacks whose inverse images cover every scheme mapping to the source. The diagonal in the definition of algebraic stack is representable by algebraic spaces.

proof.text: Fix P from the five properties. On schemes, its composition laws are respectively [lem-trf-smooth-composition], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), [lem-pc-flat-compose], [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). The chart operations additionally use arbitrary scheme base change for etaleness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. All these laws concern arbitrary schemes, so source charts need not be Noetherian or quasi-compact. The completed stack base-change proof in step 4 uses formal test reassociation rather than a scheme base-change law for P.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], this $P$ is etale local on source-and-target. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] to interpret it on algebraic spaces: it holds on every etale scheme presentation exactly when it holds on one presentation covering the source. We will use both directions, and the scheme comparison, below. This supplies chart independence; it is not an assumption that a chosen smooth stack atlas is etale.

Here are the fibre-product identifications and chart operations used below. Fibre products of algebraic spaces exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A map from a scheme $U$ to a space $F$ is representable: for another scheme $T\to F$, $U\times_F T$ is the pullback of the representable diagonal of $F$ along $U\times_S T\to F\times_S F$, so is a scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For the chart operations we use only representable etale maps (scheme-valued tests). For such $a:A\to B$ and $b:B\to C$, a scheme test $T\to C$ factors their composite as the etale scheme maps $A_T\to B_T\to T$; step 1 gives etaleness of the composite. If the two maps are surjective, these scheme maps are surjective and [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] applies. Arbitrary base change retains exactly the same scheme tests; base changes of an etale surjective scheme map are etale by step 1 and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Hence these operations preserve representable etale charts and their covering property. In all ensuing 2-pullback reassociations the functor keeps the maps to the factors and composes the displayed isomorphisms between their images; its inverse inserts the identity isomorphism at the repeated factor. Thus these reassociations are equivalences of the explicit groupoids of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], compatible with all projections.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), presentation refinements; algebraic.tex Tags 0302 and 045C, formal pullback reassociation

proof.text: For a scheme test t:T→H of the base change H×_G F→H, insert the repeated H factor and its identity comparison to define T×_G F→T×_H(H×_G F). It is fully faithful because the outer comma square forces the middle component of each arrow to be t applied to its T component. For essential surjectivity, an object (a,(h,x,β),α) is isomorphic to the inserted object with comparison g(α) followed by β; the isomorphism has components identity on a, α on h, and identity on x. The functor preserves the projection to T strictly. Composing each space-test equivalence with this functor retains the same representing space, projection, and chart property. Thus arbitrary stack base change preserves ModuliSpaceTest P for any scheme property P; forgetting its chart clause gives representability. This proves the base-change theorem directly from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

For composition, take a scheme test of g with its property witness B→T. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-composite-chart-refinement] to get the representing space A of gf and pointwise compatible refinements of each étale chart U→A. For each x∈U its refinement passes through a scheme chart W→B and through a chart V→M of a scheme test of f on W. The two existing ModuliSpaceTest hypotheses give P(V→W) and P(W→T). Apply the scheme composition instance for the selected property P to get P(V→T). The equality of projections in the refinement lemma gives the étale local witnesses for P(U→T), with identity target chart. The locality clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] descends P to U→T. This works for every chart, giving ModuliSpaceTest P (gf). Forgetting its property clause supplies representability.

source.place: Tags 0300 (lemma-base-change-by-space-representable-by-space), 045B (lemma-composition-representable-transformations-property), and 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target): the property-independent iterated-test and compatible-chart construction in steps 3 and 7 of lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus.

proof.text: Let $\{\mathcal X_i\subset\mathcal X\}$ be an open cover and keep $f$ representable by spaces. For a scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, write $A=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ and choose an etale scheme atlas $U\to A$. Its inverse images $U_i$ of the open substacks are open subschemes covering $U$, by the meaning of open substack and [def-weil-open-immersion]. The maps $U_i\to A_i=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ are etale charts by step 3. If all $f|_{\mathcal X_i}$ have $P$, their scheme tests and step 2 give $P(U_i\to T)$. Open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). The source-cover clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] gives $P(U\to T)$, and step 2 gives $P(A\to T)$. Conversely if $f$ has $P$, any chart of $A_i$ composed with $A_i\to A$ is an etale chart (the latter map pulls back to open subschemes, hence etale by the same scheme lemma). Step 2 gives $P$ on that chart, hence on $A_i\to T$. To justify representability here before using the tests, $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ is representable by schemes by the definition of open substack; [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space] applied over $A$ makes $A_i=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}A$ a space. Thus $P$ is local on an open cover of the source.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target) and descent.tex Tag 04R1(f); stacks-properties.tex Section 04XB; restriction to open source substacks

proof.text: The implications are checked on exactly the same scheme charts and with exactly the same algebraic-space base-change witnesses. Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Etale supplies Etale→Smooth [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The scheme instances [lem-pc-smooth-flat] give Smooth→Flat and Smooth→LocallyOfFinitePresentation. The finite-presentation scheme instance gives LocallyOfFinitePresentation→LocallyOfFiniteType [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Applying these instances to each chart proves all four implications, without the fibre-dimension assertion of lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres and without changing a presentation.

Use the field-extension lifting meaning of surjectivity. This argument applies to arbitrary stack morphisms, whether or not representable. If $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is surjective and $x'$ is an object of $\mathcal Y'$ over a field $K$, lift its image in $\mathcal Y$ after $K\hookrightarrow L$ to an object $x$ of $\mathcal X$ and an isomorphism $f(x)\simeq x'|_L$. The triple $(x'|_L,x,\phi)$ is an object of $\mathcal Y'\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ over $L$ lifting $x'$. For two surjective composable maps, lift first over $K\hookrightarrow L$ through the second map, then over $L\hookrightarrow M$ through the first. Restriction and composition of the two isomorphisms gives a lift of the original object over $M$. These constructions use exactly the 2-fibre product of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and prove surjectivity under arbitrary base change and composition. The assertions include empty targets: there is then no field-valued object to lift.

Let $U=\coprod_iU_i$ be the scheme supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], in the universe required by [def-weil-size-convention]. Its summands give a disjoint open cover. The maps $q_i$ are objects of $\mathcal X(U_i)$ by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. On distinct overlaps the base is empty, and stack descent for the empty cover identifies the fibre over the empty scheme with the terminal groupoid; hence the restrictions have a unique overlap isomorphism, satisfying the cocycle equation. Effective descent on the disjoint open cover gives an object over $U$ restricting to these objects. It defines $q:U\to\mathcal X$, with specified 2-isomorphisms $q|_{U_i}\simeq q_i$. This is a descent construction of the map to a stack; the ordinary scheme coproduct universal property is used only to construct the source.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), preliminary disjoint-source construction using stack descent; stacks.tex definition of effective object descent

proof.text: For a scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the 2-fibre product $U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ along the scheme $U\times_ST\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$. Indeed both groupoids consist of maps to $U,T$ with an isomorphism between their images; this is the tuple description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Since the diagonal of the algebraic stack is representable by spaces, its scheme pullback is a space. Thus $q$ is representable by spaces without any assertion that an arbitrary disjoint union of spaces is already constructed. Apply the source-locality result of step 8 to the open cover $U=\bigcup_iU_i$: each restriction is the given etale $q_i$, so $q$ is etale. For the empty index set, descent gives the unique object over the empty scheme and the same empty-cover argument in step 8 applies.

proof.text: Here is the comparison of the two surjectivity conventions for $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ representable by algebraic spaces. For a scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ put $A=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, an algebraic space, and recall from step 3 that maps from schemes to $A$ are representable. Suppose $f$ is surjective in the field-lifting sense, and let $U\to A$ be any surjective etale scheme chart and $t\in T$. Restrict the object of $\mathcal Y$ over $T$ to $y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$; lifting gives $\kappa(t)\hookrightarrow L$, an object $x$ of $\mathcal X$ over $L$ and $\phi:f(x)\simeq y|_L$. By the tuple description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], $(x,\operatorname{Spec}L\to T,\phi)$ is a map $s:\operatorname{Spec}L\to A$ whose composite to $T$ has image $t$. The scheme $U\times_{A,s}\operatorname{Spec}L$ maps surjectively onto $\operatorname{Spec}L$ by the definition of a surjective representable map in [def-trf-algebraic-space], so it has a point; its image $u\in U$ maps to $t$. Hence $U\to T$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Conversely suppose that for each scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ some surjective etale scheme chart $U\to A$ has $U\to T$ surjective. For an object $y$ of $\mathcal Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ take $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and such a chart $U$ (a chart exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]). As $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is surjective, $U$ has a point $u$; put $L=\kappa(u)\supseteq K$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U\to A$ is, by the same tuple description, an object $x$ of $\mathcal X$ over $L$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and an isomorphism $f(x)\simeq y|_L$: the required lift. Thus the field-lifting condition, the chart test for every chart and the chart test for one chart per $T$ are equivalent, and step 10 applies in either reading; empty $T$ and empty $\mathcal Y$ are included.
